_comment: Provenance for every value in this directory. Each corpus file names its source by key. Nothing here is committed to the page: this is the evidence store that a future tool reads. Values were transcribed from primary files or primary text, never from a summarising model.

mext-2020.title: Standard Tables of Food Composition in Japan, 2020 (Eighth Revised Edition)
mext-2020.publisher: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT), Japan

components_used.FIB-SDFS: low molecular weight soluble fibre, g (AOAC 2011.25)
components_used.FIB-SDFP: high molecular weight soluble fibre, g (AOAC 2011.25)

limitations: Single figures with no n or SD published in the main table, so ranges cannot be derived from this source alone.
Japanese samples. Iodine, molybdenum and chromium in plants track soil, so these are not UK values.
Hijiki rows distinguish stainless steel from iron cooking vessels; other rows do not state vessel.

afcd-r3.title: Australian Food Composition Database, Release 3
limitations: FSANZ states of its own chromium data: 'Levels appear to be highly variable and values presented in this database should be used with caution.' Independent corroboration of the chromium contamination problem.
Oligosaccharides (undifferentiated) are reported for cereal bars and processed foods only, and are generally imputed or borrowed. Do not use as analytical values.
Blank and zero are not distinguished as cleanly as in MEXT: absence of a value is a blank cell, but a reported 0 may be an assumed zero.
No soluble/insoluble fibre split; total dietary fibre only.

ifct-2017.title: Indian Food Composition Tables 2017
ifct-2017.authors: Longvah T., Ananthan R., Bhaskarachary K., Venkaiah K.
ifct-2017.publisher: National Institute of Nutrition, Indian Council of Medical Research, Hyderabad
tables_extracted: Table 11: Oligosaccharides, Phytosterols, Saponins and Phytates (p.403), 304 rows
Table 9: Organic Acids (p.313), 312 rows, including oxalate reported as total, soluble AND insoluble
ifct-2017.note_oxalate: Table 9 splits oxalate into soluble and insoluble. Only the soluble fraction binds calcium in the gut, and the split is large: sesame (gingelly) seeds carry 2156 mg total oxalate but only 78.6 mg soluble, while black cardamom carries 2472 mg total and 1471 mg soluble. A total-oxalate figure alone would misrepresent both. Blank cells in this table mean below detectable limit, per the table's own header note.
ifct-2017.reports: mean with n and standard deviation, sampled compositely from six regions of India
limitations: Values are for foods as purchased, generally dry or raw. This page's legumes are cooked, and the raffinose family leaches into cooking water, so these must not be applied to cooked rows without a stated conversion.
Indian cultivars and Indian soils.

Extracted from PDF text by column position. Anchors are read from each page's own header row because the layout shifts between pages; an early global-anchor version silently shifted phytosterols one column left and was discarded. Parsed rows were verified against the raw text for eight foods.
304 of 528 foods parsed. Rows whose names wrap awkwardly may still be missing.
Table 9 IS now extracted (312 rows). Table 1 (fibre fractions), Table 6 (starch and individual sugars) and Table 10 (polyphenols) are NOT yet extracted.

cofid-2021.title: McCance and Widdowson's The Composition of Foods Integrated Dataset (CoFID), 2021
cofid-2021.publisher: Public Health England / Food Standards Agency
limitations: Oligosaccharide is a lumped total with no breakdown into raffinose, stachyose or verbascose.
Oligosaccharide is populated for 363 of 2887 foods; biotin for 1925.
No chromium, molybdenum, boron, taurine, inulin, beta-glucan, pectin or soluble/insoluble fibre column exists in CoFID.
Foods join by UK food codes, so any link to this page's rows is a reviewed name match, never an id join.

usda-foundation-2025.title: USDA FoodData Central, Foundation Foods

measured_here.boron (1137): 17 foods, all dry beans at 0% moisture

limitations: Boron values are all 'Beans, Dry, X (0% moisture)', a dry-matter basis that cannot be converted to a cooked row without assuming hydration and no leaching.
Chromium (1096), taurine (1234), inulin (1403) and pectin (1017) have ZERO rows.
Foundation Foods uses different FDC ids from SR Legacy and does not join to it by id.

usda-sr-legacy-2018.title: USDA FoodData Central, SR Legacy
usda-sr-legacy-2018.note: Measured this session: nutrient ids for chromium (1096), molybdenum (1102), boron (1137), biotin (1176), taurine (1234), inulin (1403), pectin (1017), beta-glucan (1068/2058), oligosaccharides (1069/2064), raffinose (1076), stachyose (1077), verbascose (2063), soluble fibre (1082) and insoluble fibre (1084) are all DEFINED but carry ZERO rows across all 7793 foods. Control counts: protein 7793, calcium 7708, vitamin E 5580, phytosterols 489.

cnf-2026.title: Canadian Nutrient File 2026
cnf-2026.note: 173 nutrients, 5690 foods. Of the components wanted here it carries only biotin (416, 116 rows) and 'Fructans (inulin)' (1001, 53 rows, mostly manufactured foods such as cookies and sandwiches). No iodine, chromium, molybdenum, boron, taurine, oxalate, phytate, and total dietary fibre only. Not extracted.

thor-2011.citation: Thor M.Y., Harnack L., King D., Jasthi B., Pettit J. (2011). Evaluation of the comprehensiveness and reliability of the chromium composition of foods in the literature. Journal of Food Composition and Analysis 24(8):1147-1152.
thor-2011.type: compilation of 1382 values across 856 foods from 51 articles, 1980-2007
thor-2011.quality: moderate as a compilation; values inherit the quality of their source studies
limitations: The authors' own conclusion: 'assigning representative chromium values to foods in a food and nutrient database may not be appropriate in this context.'
Only 39% of NCC core foods could be assigned a chromium value.
Medians sit far below means, because means are dragged by contaminated outliers.

reczajska-2005.citation: Ręczajska W., Jędrzejczak R., Szteke B. (2005). Determination of chromium content of food and beverages of plant origin. Polish Journal of Food and Nutrition Sciences 14/55(2):183-188.
reczajska-2005.method: ZETAAS, electrothermal AAS with Zeeman background correction
reczajska-2005.qa: CRM CTA-VTL-2 Virginia Tobacco Leaves; recovery 94-104%; RSD 1.2-3.7%
reczajska-2005.note: Thor 2011 cites this paper with the author name misspelled as 'Raczajska'. The strawberry range prints in the PDF as '61-34' and is actually 6-134 ug/kg, confirmed against the paper's own Table 7 province ranges.

laidlaw-1990.citation: Laidlaw S.A., Grosvenor M., Kopple J.D. (1990). The taurine content of common foodstuffs. Journal of Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition 14:183-188.
laidlaw-1990.finding: Taurine assayed in 48 plant foods and not detected in any. A finding of absence, not a gap.
laidlaw-1990.caveat: Red algae are the documented exception. Porphyra (nori) has been measured at about 4.11 mg/g dry matter, so 'plants contain no taurine' is wrong for the nori and kelp rows.

van-loo-1995.citation: van Loo J., Coussement P., de Leenheer L., Hoebregs H., Smits G. (1995). On the presence of inulin and oligofructose as natural ingredients in the western diet. Critical Reviews in Food Science and Nutrition 35(6):525-552.
van-loo-1995.type: the canonical inulin and oligofructose food table
van-loo-1995.status: NOT yet extracted. Superseded in usefulness for this page by AFCD, which publishes analytical inulin for 50 foods including this page's grains and legumes.

usda-iodine-r4.title: USDA, FDA and ODS-NIH Database for the Iodine Content of Common Foods, Release 4.0
usda-iodine-r4.publisher: USDA ARS / FDA / NIH Office of Dietary Supplements
usda-iodine-r4.reports: n, mean, SD, min, max, source and years analysed per food
usda-iodine-r4.join: carries NDB / SR Legacy and Foundation Foods ids, so it joins to this page by id rather than by name. Same key tools/flavonoids.mjs already uses.
usda-iodine-r4.key_finding: Resolves the oats iodine conflict. Cooked oatmeal 0.2 ug/100 g, n=10, max 1.1. Brown rice cooked 0 ug, n=28, min 0, max 0. With MEXT also reporting not-detected, AFCD's 74 ug for rolled oats and 9.8 for brown rice are outliers by two to three orders of magnitude, not geographic variation.
limitations: US samples.
Iodised salt dominates several processed categories; pasta boiled in iodised salt reads 22.4 ug against 0 for whole wheat pasta cooked without.

frida-6.1.title: Frida, the Danish Food Composition Database, version 6.1
frida-6.1.reports: value, min, max, median, number of determinations and source per value. The richest per-value provenance of any database here.
frida-6.1.key_finding: Unblocks boron, but by 21 values rather than 49. Its boron is on a normal fresh-weight basis rather than the 0% moisture dry beans that made the USDA Foundation Foods boron unusable. Wheat germ 250 ug (n=7) and wheat bran 270 (n=10) stand; buckwheat groats 530 is n=0 from FINKOST 1986 and is refused. See FRIDA-PROVENANCE.md.
limitations: Danish samples and Danish soils.

A mean can sit below its own min: the mean divides by every determination while min and max span only the detections above the limit, so it counts non-detects as zero and understates. Marked partial, not corrected.
Two molybdenum rows, both corn flakes, report min=20 against max=3. Refused as malformed.

A mean can sit below its own min: it divides by every determination while min and max span only the detections above the limit, so it counts non-detects as zero and understates. Marked partial, not corrected.
Two molybdenum rows, both corn flakes, report min=20 against max=3. Refused as malformed.
Rebuilt from the published workbook by tools/extract_frida.mjs. The workbook is not committed; fetch it from the DOI into tools/cache/.
frida-6.1.provenance: Every value carries a number of determinations and a named source, and the published source table names all 502. That separates Frida's own analytical work from the foreign tables it compiled. Of 873 biotin values 473 are admitted; the rest are borrowed from another food (146), undetermined (209) or compiled (45). Source 1344 is McCance and Widdowson 4th edition, of which CoFID is the 7th; sources 2141, 2145 and 2289 are CoFID, AFCD and the CNF, all already cited here directly. The admission rule is in tools/frida.mjs.
frida-6.1.licence: CC BY 4.0, checked 2026-08-19 against the dataset's own Readme sheet and the DTU Data record. Redistribution of derived values is permitted with attribution. Required credit: "The Danish Food Composition Database (http://fcdb.fooddata.dk), version 6.1, May 2026. The Food Institute, Technical University of Denmark." Only the documentation PDFs are all rights reserved; both data files are CC-BY 4.0.

phenol-explorer.title: Phenol-Explorer, database on polyphenol content in foods
phenol-explorer.reports: mean, min, max, SD, n, number of publications, publication ids and PubMed ids per value. 5055 of the stored rows carry a PubMed id. An earlier version of this note called that the best provenance of any source here; see the limitations, because it is traceability rather than quality and one of the ids is wrong.
phenol-explorer.quality: high as a compilation, and not independent of usda-flavonoids-r33 for the flavonoid columns
phenol-explorer.note: Alcoholic beverages excluded on extraction. Adds lignans and stilbenes, neither of which the page carries. Also carries a total polyphenols figure; note the page deliberately has no total flavonoid column, and the reasoning there does not automatically transfer. Its own publication list is held beside it in phenol-explorer-publications.json, because the composition download references papers by id and never names them.
limitations: A compilation of published analyses, so values span methods and decades; the method group is recorded per row and must be carried through.

NOT A SECOND SOURCE for the flavonoid columns. It and USDA Flavonoid Release 3.3 compiled the same literature: 143 of the 178 cells a page map would fill share at least one publication with USDA's own reference list for the same food, chiefly Hertog 1992, Justesen 1998, Harnly 2006 and Lugasi and Hovari 2000 and 2002. Its pecan is USDA's pecan to one decimal on all eight compounds. Check with `node tools/phenol_explorer.mjs overlap` before citing it beside USDA.

The PubMed ids are not reliable. All 121 rows citing publication 655, which its own publication list gives as Harnly 2006 (PMID 17177529), carry PMID 22327611, a 2012 review of diet and endothelial function that measured no food. The mismatch is upstream in composition-data.xlsx, not in this ingest, and was confirmed against a fresh download.

Two chromatography methods, and the choice changes a figure by an order of magnitude: the plain rows report the free aglycone and the hydrolysis rows the aglycone total. Blackberry quercetin is 0 by the first and 0.87 by the second. Only the hydrolysis rows compare with USDA.

assessed-lower-value._comment: Downloaded and checked, little or nothing to add beyond what is already held.
assessed-lower-value.ciqual-2025: France, 3484 foods. Of the wanted components carries iodine and total organic acids only.
assessed-lower-value.nevo-2025: Netherlands. Of the wanted components carries iodine only. Has explicit conditions-of-use terms.
assessed-lower-value.fineli-rel20: Finland, 75 components. Carries chromium, iodine, molybdenum, insoluble fibre, organic acids and individual sugars. No biotin. Overlaps sources already held.
assessed-lower-value.tbca-brazil: Supplied as PDFs covering carbohydrate profile, glycaemic response, flavonoids and carotenoids. Not extracted; flavonoids and carotenoids overlap existing columns.

fao-phytate.title: FAO/INFOODS/IZiNCG Global Food Composition Database for Phytate, Version 1.0 (PhyFoodComp1.0)
fao-phytate.publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

usda-flavonoids-r33.title: USDA Database for the Flavonoid Content of Selected Foods, Release 3.3
usda-flavonoids-r33.note: A compilation of published analyses, not a laboratory programme, though USDA's own Harnly 2006 is the single largest contributor. It says which paper each figure came from, and that list is extracted to usda-flavonoids-references.json by `node tools/flavonoids.mjs refs`. Ask it before treating any other polyphenol database as a second source: Phenol-Explorer shares 143 of 178 candidate cells' provenance with it.
